subject: octopus
pitch: A curious reef octopus in coral and rust tones, covered in little bumps and paler mottling. A soft, bulbous head, golden eyes with bar-shaped pupils and a slightly grumpy brow. Its eight arms curl out in every direction, each lined with rows of cream suckers, and one arm proudly holds up an old brass key it found on a shipwreck.
reasoning:
I'm sketching out the plan for a three.js octopus module, sizing the mantle and arms to realistic reef octopus proportions, and setting up a seeded random generator plus materials for a coral-colored body with rust bumps and mottled texture.

For the geometry itself, I'm placing bumpy spheres on a scaled mantle shape, adding golden eyes with dark bar-shaped pupils and grumpy brows, then generating eight tapering tentacle chains that spiral outward from the mantle base with small sucker discs along the underside of each arm.

I'm deciding to build each arm as a sequence of overlapping spheres with decreasing radius rather than a constant-radius tube, to get a tapered look, and computing sucker placement along the arm using tangent and side vectors at each point.

Writing arm curve math...

For the resting pose I'll let arms spread loosely around the floor, and for the arm holding the key I'll give it a raised lift so its tip curves upward distinctly from the others.

The key itself gets a brass torus ring, cylindrical shaft, and boxy teeth, oriented vertically and nestled into the grip of the raised tip. I'll compute the whole octopus's bounding box afterward and shift the group down and centered so the lowest point touches the ground exactly at y=0. For texture, I'm planning to draw a mottled coral base color with pale blotches onto a canvas and use it as a CanvasTexture on the mantle and body surfaces.

Now I'm scattering small rust-colored bump spheres across the upper hemisphere of the ellipsoidal mantle, computing surface points by scaling random directions against the mantle's radii, then pushing them slightly outward along the normal. I'm also positioning the arm bases around the lower mantle and placing the golden eyes with flattened pupils oriented outward from the mantle surface using normalized direction vectors.

I'm settling on a color palette — coral body, rust shadows, cream suckers, brass accents, gold eyes with dark pupils — and deciding the arms and mantle share the same textured material. Now I'm setting up a seeded random number generator and starting to write the actual component code.

Writing component code...

Defining materials next, then working through the body geometry: the mantle ellipsoid, scattered bumps using a surface-point/normal approximation, bulging eyes with pupils and grumpy tilted brows, and curling tentacle arms built from tapered sphere chains with suckers positioned using tangent/ventral/side vectors. I'm also designing a small key prop held in one arm's tip, then grounding the whole octopus by computing its bounding box and shifting the root so it rests centered on the floor. Finally I'm sanity-checking mesh and triangle counts to stay within budget before writing out the complete implementation.
